solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Money a laboratory's cut for water vessel

indicators.note: the lab has cut into the money, so the word for money is split open to take the other letters

parts.note: cash is money
lab is short for laboratory; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped lab has its funding slashed, apparently in the market for a water vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' reads as a budget cut in the surface, but here it means the lab letters slice into the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd hollowed out and dried to serve as a container for water.

clue.text: Unfinished gateau gets stored initially in container

indicators.note: in places the stored letter within the shortened cake
unfinished means the word for gateau loses its final letter

parts.note: a gateau is a rich cake

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of stored is used

explanation.surface: A half-eaten gateau is put away in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims CAKE to CAK; 'initially' takes S from 'stored'; 'in' puts S inside, giving CA-S-K.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a barrel, a kind of container for liquids such as wine or beer.

clue.text: Take a dive unclothed for a breather

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of its outer covering, so the word for take a dive loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to plunge is to take a dive

explanation.surface: A swimmer strips off and dives in for a breath of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclothed' strips the outside letters P and E from PLUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lung is the organ you breathe with, so it is literally a breather.

clue.text: Cricketers dine when short of time in place close to The Oval

parts.note: batters are cricketers who bat

indicators.note: short of means the word for dine is lacking the letter for time

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Cricket players have dinner in a rush near the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; BATTERSEA is a nearby district of south London. 'when short of' removes T from EAT, leaving EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district of south London lying a short distance from the Oval cricket ground in Kennington.

clue.text: Ruling starts on this weight of cake

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds
a scone is a small plain cake

explanation.surface: A baker's riddle: someone is told the weight of a cake, as if a reign depended on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is a British unit of weight (14 lb); a SCONE is a small British teacake.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish and British monarchs have been crowned seated over this coronation stone, so a reign begins on it.

clue.text: I work in charge of pursuing British film

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the other pieces come after the letter for British

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of directing work in pursuit of a British movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical motion picture, a movie telling someone's life story.

clue.text: Does nothing with days in French islands

indicators.note: in puts the letter for days within the French word

parts.note: îles is the French word for islands

explanation.surface: Someone lazes about for days on islands off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside ILES, the French for 'islands'.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be inactive, so someone who idles is doing nothing at all.

clue.text: Homer's resting place is suspect if long associated with poet

indicators.note: suspect is used as an adjective meaning dodgy, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scholars doubt the burial place of the poet Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges IF LONG with POET. The Homer here is a homing pigeon, not the Greek poet the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, and it roosts in a loft built for the birds.

clue.text: Devote seconds breaking into ice cream van that's old?

indicators.note: breaking into puts the letter for seconds inside the word for ice cream

parts.note: a cone is an ice cream served in a wafer cornet
a crate is slang for an old, ramshackle vehicle

explanation.surface: A thief breaks into an old ice cream van in a matter of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'ice cream van', but 'ice cream' and 'van that's old' are separate pieces; an old banger of a car is a British 'crate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to dedicate something solemnly, especially to a sacred purpose.

clue.text: Authorise second armed conflict around November

indicators.note: around means the word for armed conflict goes round the letter for November

parts.note: action is fighting, armed conflict
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A government approves a second war at around the month of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts ACTION round N, giving ANCTION after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official permission or approval for something.

clue.text: Marker on wine bottle

parts.note: a flag is a marker, as on a golf green or a map

explanation.surface: A label is stuck on a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug used for holding wine or cider.

clue.text: I turn rowboat around for fish

indicators.note: around is read as all around, in any order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An angler spins a small boat round to go after fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'around' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow trout is a species of freshwater game fish with a pinkish stripe.

clue.text: Army commanders hurried where supplies could be had

parts.note: generals command armies
tore means rushed or hurried

explanation.surface: Senior officers rushed to the place where provisions were stocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A general store is a shop selling a wide range of goods, often in a small town.

clue.text: Timepieces changing ring, first to one, then a different sound

indicators.note: different means the remaining ring letter is changed to the letter a as well
changing means a letter of the timepieces is swapped for another, the first one becoming the letter for one

parts.note: two clocks are timepieces
O looks like a ring
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clockmaker swaps parts on two clocks and hears a changed tick.
explanation.walkthrough: In CLOCK CLOCK, 'changing' turns the first O (ring) into I (one), then 'different' turns the second O into A, giving CLICK CLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Click-clack imitates a repeated sharp clicking noise, such as heels on a pavement.

clue.text: Very bad men tear into unfinished home

indicators.note: into puts the letters for men and tear inside the shortened home
unfinished means the word for home loses its final letter

parts.note: a house is a home
OR, other ranks, is crossword shorthand for ordinary soldiers or men
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: Men tear into a half-built house and wreck it.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the standard crossword shorthand for 'men'; the inserted letters go after the first letter of the shortened home.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrendous means dreadful or appalling, which is extremely bad.

clue.text: Left that southern city of France

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: Someone departed from a city in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: LYONS is the traditional English spelling of Lyon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyons is the English name for Lyon, France's third-largest city.

clue.text: Railway diversion crucial for reconstruction after constant cancellation?

parts.note: fun is entertainment, a diversion

indicators.note: for reconstruction means the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
cancellation means the letter for constant is struck out of the word crucial

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A rail diversion is crucial while a line is rebuilt after a constant stream of cancelled trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancellation' removes one C from CRUCIAL, leaving RUCIAL, which 'for reconstruction' rearranges into ICULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable railway up a steep slope, with ascending and descending cars balancing each other.

clue.text: Funny cartoon about jolly diver

indicators.note: about means the rearranged cartoon goes round the letters for jolly
funny suggests the word cartoon is made odd, its letters rearranged

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A comic cartoon features a cheerful diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is old British naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cormorant is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Meat and fish for a judge in Corsican capital

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, the fish taking the place of a judge

parts.note: Ajaccio is the capital of Corsica
J is the abbreviation for judge, so a judge gives AJ
carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A meal of meat and fish is served to a judge in Corsica's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps AJ out of AJACCIO and puts CARP in its place, leaving CARP plus ACCIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is an Italian dish of very thin slices of raw beef.

clue.text: I fret about what might recycle junk

indicators.note: about means the letters of I fret are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worries over what could be done with old rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A junk is also a Chinese sailing ship, not just rubbish, and an overhaul could restore one.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a ship's overhaul and repair, which could put an old Chinese sailing vessel back into service.

clue.text: Disapproval of Conservative Democrat leading country

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the party letters come before the word for country

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A political observer frowns on a coalition running the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Britain's 2010 Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition, nicknamed the ConDems.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemnation is strong censure, the expression of severe disapproval.

clue.text: English low-fat cream

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for low-fat or light products

explanation.surface: A tub of English reduced-fat cream on a supermarket shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' is not dairy here but means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, just as an elite is the best of a group.

clue.text: Nearly perfect suggestion

indicators.note: nearly means the word for perfect falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: Someone praises a proposal as almost flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or proposal put forward, which is a suggestion.

clue.text: May I ask you to settle in advance when record's coming out?

indicators.note: coming out means the letters for the record leave the word for settle in advance

parts.note: to prepay is to settle a bill in advance
an EP is an extended-play record; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A shopper politely asks to pay up front when a record is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' removes EP from PREPAY. 'Pray' as an old polite request, as in 'pray tell', means 'may I ask you'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old-fashioned speech the single word serves as a polite request, as in 'tell me, I beg', which means please may I ask.

clue.text: Trouble with serious offence over good-looking youth

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: over means the word for serious offence is turned over, written back to front

parts.note: a sin is a serious offence

explanation.surface: A handsome young man is in trouble for a grave crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, names any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: What will strain old spacecraft chasing the speed of light

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the old spacecraft follows the letter for the speed of light

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
a lander is a spacecraft that touches down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: An ageing spacecraft strains to keep up with the speed of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts O plus LANDER after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated kitchen bowl used to drain or strain food.

clue.text: Fate is satisfied by king

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter for king stands next to the other pieces, in front

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
met, as in met a demand, means satisfied

explanation.surface: A king is content with his destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, from a Turkish word for one's lot.

clue.text: Statistics with January not showing the first three figures

parts.note: stat is short for statistic, as in stats

indicators.note: not showing the first three means the opening three letters of January are hidden away

explanation.surface: A report presents statistics for January minus the first three numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not showing the first three' drops JAN from JANUARY, leaving UARY. 'figures' looks like numbers but means sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is statues collectively, so sculpted figures make it up.
